title.narrative: DEC East Africa Drought Appeal Project Diocese of Maralal 2011-2012

description.narrative: Current La Nina Induced drought and high food prices has affected over 10 million people across Horn and East Africa. In Kenya, the government and UN indicate that over 3.5 million people are affected and in dire need of humanitarian assistance . Samburu North and East Districts are Arid areas in Rift Valley province of Kenya with 110,801 inhabitants, over 80% of the population depend on livestock as a means of livelihood and primary source of food. Following the failure of short ( October 2010) and Long rains (March to May 2011) most of the pastrolists have lost their livestock, Distance to water points has increased from an average of 8km to about 40kms, the few agropastrolists in the area experienced massive crop failure. Diocese of Maralal which has been monitoring the effects of drought in the area conducted a rapid assessment between 23 and 30th of June 2010 to prioritize intervention areas. the assessment finding show that most households do not have food 90% of 300 interviewed households had only 1 meal in the last three days , distance to water points have dramatically increased and resource based conflict have increased. In Conjuction with CAFOD the Diocese has designed an emergency drought response project targeting 5506 households in Wamba, Nkaroni, Naimirimo Ngilai, Waso, baragoi, Nachola, Elbarata, Nyiro Parkati and Kawop divisions in Samburu North and East district. The project aims at mitigating the effects of the current drought in Samburu East and North by promoting access to food and water in the first 6 months followed by 18 months recovery phase that will focusing on rebuilding community resilince and reducing the impact of future drought. The 1st phase will ensure access to safe water to 5506 HH through construction of a borehole, desilting of 7 water pans, provision of food aid to 669 HH to ensure poor and unproductive households have access to food assistance .Recovery activities will be identified within 4 months of the start of the six months of implementation of the 1st phase relief activities.
